newsitem.title: USA: Stone Energy reserves rose 49 pct.
newsitem.headline: Stone Energy reserves rose 49 pct.

text.p: Stone Energy Corp said Wednesday its proved oil and natural gas reserves increased 49 percent in the first eight months of the year.
The company also said its credit facility with a bank group led by NationsBank of Texas NA was amended last month, increasing the total credit available to $125 million from $80 million.

Stone Energy said it intends to pursue an underwritten public equity offering during the fourth quarter to retire the $45 million term loan now outstanding under the credit line and to provide capital for the future development of its property base.

Stone Energy said its proved oil reserves totaled 10.5 million barrels on August 31, up 31 percent from the 8.0 million estimated as of December 31, 1995, and natural gas rserves were up 59 percent to 128.9 billion cubic feet from 81.2 billion at year end.
Reserves attributable to acquisitions closed in August and September are included in these amounts and comprise 27 percent of the August 31 total, the company said.
During the first eight months of 1996, Stone said, it produced some 0.9 million barrels of oil and 7.9 billion cubic feet of gas.
Based on the new reserve estimates, the company said its reserve replacement rate for this period was 570 percent.

It said the amended credit facility is comprised of a three-year revolving credit loan and a one-year term loan. Current availability of the facility is $105 million, and the current weighted average interest rate of the facility is 7.9 percent per annum. As of September 30, the total outstanding principal balance was $84.6 million and letters of credit totaling $6.6 million had been issued.

The revolver provides for total availability of $80 million with a limitation on total outstanding borrowings based on a borrowing base amount established by the banks for the company's oil and gas properties, which currently is $60 million, Stone Energy said.

The term loan of $45 million was established to finance the closing of the recent acquisitions and development costs incurred during the third quarter. If the term loan is outstanding on January 31, 1997, the banks have the right to redetermine the borrowing base of the facility which could result in an acceleration of the payments due under the term loan, Stone Energy said. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
